advice.title: Lowering your risk of BP, diabetes and cancer
advice.text: Stop tobacco in every form, including gutka and khaini, and avoid alcohol. Be physically active for at least 150 minutes a week, for example 30 minutes a day on 5 days. Keep your waist size down. Get your BP and blood sugar checked every year, and your mouth, breasts and cervix screened every 5 years, even if you feel well.

advice.title: When to get tested for TB
advice.text: If you have a cough for more than 2 weeks, blood in your sputum, fever for more than 2 weeks, weight loss or night sweats, come back and give a sputum sample for a free TB test. Tell us if anyone in your family has TB.

advice.title: Care in pregnancy
advice.text: Eat about a quarter more food than usual, including a variety of foods, and use iodised salt. Rest for 2 hours in the day and 8 hours at night. Take the iron-folic acid and calcium tablets exactly as prescribed. Attend every antenatal check-up and plan your delivery in a hospital.

advice.title: Danger signs in pregnancy
advice.text: Go to the nearest hospital at once if you have bleeding, high fever, severe tiredness or breathlessness, headache with blurred vision, fits or swelling all over the body, leaking of water, labour pains before time or for more than 12 hours, or if the baby moves less than usual.
